topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning objectives, and frames the central question of what causes cancer.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, mutation sources, and epidemiological risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual framework of cancer development by examining how intrinsic biological mutations, environmental exposures, and population-level epidemiological variations shape cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral mechanisms in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how bacterial, parasitic, and viral pathogens contribute to malignant transformation, illustrated through the multi-factorial case of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and xenobiotic metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which dietary toxins, UV radiation, and environmental chemicals undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and multi-step carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the role of non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and developmental stage-specific tissue susceptibility in driving tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Experimental and epidemiological methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the genomic signatures, epidemiological cohort designs, and in vivo and in vitro testing methods used to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit evaluation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing everyday carcinogenic risk and exposure decisions within a practical risk-versus-benefit perspective.
